problem: The sentence giving the left-sided case is garbled: "and gives −e^(−at)u(−t) when Re(s)0." The inequality is broken, so the condition for the left-sided inverse is missing. A student cannot tell which ROC gives −e^(−at)u(−t).
The note "p_k is positive when the pole is at −p_k" is vague and reads like a condition on p_k rather than a definition of the pole location. Students may think p_k must be positive.
fix: "p_k is the pole location with the sign flipped: the pole sits at s = −p_k, and p_k itself may be positive, negative or zero."

problem: The last node is labelled x(t) but its note gives only the ROC ("ROC Re(s)>−1"), not the time function the flowchart is supposed to end with. The reader has to jump back to the text to see the result.
fix: Put the result in the note, for example "x(t) = (e^(−t)+2e^(−3t))u(t)", and keep the ROC as a second remark or in the figure caption.
